extracted.intended_audience: design and patent applicants, IP attorneys, examiners, and other practitioners operating under Turkish patent and design law
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and evaluative standards from the Turkish code governing design oppositions, ownership, renewal, invalidity, infringement, and patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) for patents and designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of publication — publication date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication date of a design for which postponement of publication has been demanded shall be the date of publication of visual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If postponement of publication is requested, the effective publication date is when the visual representation is published. Related obligations (e.g., notifying defendants to enable suits within postponement duration) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to defendant during postponement
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in the registry and the application file must be notified to the defendant to ensure that an infringement could be sued within the postponement duration of the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registry/application-file information must be provided to the defendant so that infringement suits remain actionable during any postponed-publication period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition time limits and grounds (designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may object to decisions within two months from notification; third parties may object in writing within three months from publication by paying the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party objections must allege that the design fails definitions in Article 55 (first and second paragraphs), fails conditions of Articles 56 and 57, falls in scope of Article 58(4) or Article 64(6)(c), was filed in bad faith, or contains unauthorized use of intellectual property rights. If the objection fee/payment proof is not timely submitted, the objection is invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions are examined by the Board; the applicant's opinion may be sought; opposing party may be requested to submit additional information and documents within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional information isn’t submitted in time, the objection is examined on existing documents. If deficiencies are found during opposition examination, operations resume from the incomplete stage and necessary decisions are published in the Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of accepted objections / partial invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third-party objection under the statutory grounds is accepted, registration of the design (or part of it) shall be deemed invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial invalidation removes only the invalidated part; the remaining portion must still meet protection conditions and preserve design identity to maintain continuity. In multiple applications, registrations not subject to objection but deemed invalid via additional documents can be ex officio invalidated per procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered design term and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of protection of a registered design covers five years from filing and may be renewed in five-year periods up to a total of twenty-five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal requests must be filed by the design owner with proof of payment of renewal fee. Renewals become effective the day after the previous protection period expires and are recorded in the register and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered design term
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of protection of unregistered designs covers three years from first presentation to the public of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered designs are protected for three years from first public disclosure; separate rules apply for enforcement (see infringement provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal deadlines and late renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for renewal shall be made within six months before expiry with proof of payment; if omitted, renewal may be requested within six months after expiry subject to additional fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely request renewal or to submit payment proof allows a six-month grace period upon payment of additional fee; renewals take effect immediately after prior term ends and are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design right ownership and transferrable nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Design right belongs to the designer or his successors and may be transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple persons are owners, joint-ownership shares are governed by agreement or, absent agreement, by joint ownership provisions in the Turkish Civil Code. Each owner can dispose of their share, use the design by notifying others, and sue for infringement (but must notify co-owners so they can join proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing decisions among joint owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Right owners must decide unanimously to grant third parties a license; if unanimity is absent, a court may equitably grant licensing authority to one or more owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court intervention can assign licensing power when co-owners cannot agree, using equitable principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on transferring/dividing application or registration
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to transfer the design application or design registration or to divide those to establish any right on them, even if more than one person becomes right owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute bars transfer or division of the application/registration for the purpose of creating subsidiary rights; details are governed by the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disseize (challenge to ownership) — remedies and time bars
rubrics_metrics.description: A person claiming to be the legal right owner may demand the court to transfer the design owner right or be recognized as owner; partial rights follow joint-ownership rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be made within three years after publication (registered) or presentation (unregistered), except where the defendant acted in bad faith (no limitation). Final decisions are registrable and published; if application is registered during proceedings, the proceeding converts into one about the registered design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects when ownership change is recorded (post-disseize)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon entry of ownership change in the registry, third-party rights relating to the design terminate; prior users may request a non-exclusive license within two months of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month period starts from Office notification of the real right owner. The license request does not apply if the prior user acted in bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees’ designs — default employer ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed, designs made by employees due to obligations in a business organization belong to the employer; similar rules apply to designs made by employees using organizational information/tools upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions also apply to students, interns and certain instructors; if design is made outside service relationship, ownership is determined by contract between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for employee/instructor designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee has the right to request a price determined by considering the importance of the design; if parties cannot agree, the court determines price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For designs by higher-education instructors, revenue sharing is determined by institution board and must give at least half of revenue to the designer.

rubrics_metrics.name: License form and default (designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design rights may be licensed in exclusive or non-exclusive form; unless agreed otherwise, licenses are non-exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In non-exclusive licenses the licensor may use the design or grant other licenses. In exclusive licenses the licensor cannot grant other licenses or use the design himself unless expressly reserved. Unless otherwise agreed, licensor cannot transfer license rights or grant sublicenses. Licensee must comply with contract terms or owner may enforce rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for unauthorized transfer or licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person later found not authorized to transfer design right or grant a license shall be liable to those concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is withdrawn/refused or registration canceled/invalid, Article 79 (invalidity effects) applies unless parties agreed otherwise. Time to seek compensation starts from the date of the final court decision forming the basis of liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation grounds (designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Court shall decide invalidity where it is proven that the design fails definitions in Article 55 (1–2), fails conditions in Articles 56/57, falls in Article 58(4) or Article 64(6)(c), was filed in bad faith or contains unauthorized use; also if right belongs to another person; or if an identical/similar design's earlier filing precedes the registered design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial invalidation is possible; after partial invalidation, remaining portion must still meet protection conditions and keep the design identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing and timing for invalidity actions (designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons concerned can request invalidity; invalidity may be claimed only by earlier right owners (where applicable) and by design right owners under Articles 70 and 73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may be instituted during protection or within five years following expiry. Proceedings are against the person registered as right owner on the registry date (registered designs) or against the claimant (unregistered designs). Notifications to registered owners are required so they can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invalidity decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidity decision has retroactive effect; protection under the Code is deemed null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final court decisions and contracts established/performed prior to invalidity are not affected. Return of fees paid under prior contracts may be requested partially or fully on an equitable basis. Final decisions are effective for everyone; Office cancels entry and publishes the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and relinquishment of design right
rubrics_metrics.description: Design right terminates when protection duration expires without renewal or when owner relinquishes the right (wholly or partially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver must be notified in writing to the Office and has effect as of the registration record date; relinquishment cannot be made without consent of registered right and license owners or a third party with registered interlocutory injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts deemed infringement of design right
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing, marketing, selling, offering, importing, using commercially, or stocking identical or similar products incorporating the design without consent; broadening rights by licensing/transferring without consent; or disseizing the design right constitute infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application has been registered and published (Article 65), the registrant may file civil action; publication is not determinative where infringer was informed of the application or acted in bad faith. Lack of registration marking on products does not preclude infringement. Unregistered designs presented to the public are also enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability general conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall be granted for inventions in all fields of technology provided the invention is new, involves an inventive step and is susceptible to industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the three statutory patentability criteria: novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter (enumerated exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods; mental acts, business activities, game plans; computer programs; aesthetic creations and works of art; presentation of information; and certain other categories are not considered inventions for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional exclusions include inventions violating public order/morality, certain biological processes relating to plant/animal varieties (with microbiological exceptions), treatment modalities including diagnostic and surgical methods, parts of the human body and gene sequences (with limited nuance), human cloning, altering genetic identity, using embryos for industrial purposes, and animals obtained by certain operations. Microbiological processes/products and products usable in excluded methods may have specific carve-outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — state of the art definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is novel if it is not included in the state of the art; state of the art covers everything accessible to society anywhere in the world before the application was submitted, by written/verbal disclosure, use or any other way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published contents of applications submitted on or after the application date and certain earlier national/PCT/European filings are considered part of the state of the art per Article 83(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention includes an inventive step if it is not obvious to the expert in the relevant area, taking the state of the art into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notably, the contents of applications/documents counted as state of the art under paragraph three are not to be considered in evaluating inventive step (per Article 83(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is susceptible to industry if it can be produced and used in any industrial area, including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability is broadly construed to include any industrial use; feasibility for production/use is the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior statements not defeating patentability (12-month grace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements made within twelve months prior to application (or priority date) by the inventor, by an authority to which the application was made (with conditions), or by a third party who obtained the information from the inventor, do not affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: disclosures by the inventor or disclosures made by an authority (if also mentioned in the inventor’s other application revealed improperly) or disclosures by third parties who obtained info from the inventor. The party invoking this protection must prove the conditions are met; consequences of paragraph 1 are not subject to time limit and can be alleged anytime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patent rights and permitted exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee may prevent others from producing, selling, using, importing goods subject to the patent, using a patented process, offering use of a patented process, and dealing in products directly obtained by a patented process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: non-commercial/special-purpose acts, experimental/trial uses, trials for drug registration (including tests), pharmacy preparations for a single prescription, use in making/running transport vehicles temporarily present (Paris Convention parties), and other specific international-agreement-based exceptions. There are special small-farmer and farmer-use exceptions governed by Law No. 5042 and further regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing indirect use (contributory infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee has a right to prevent supply of factors or equipment that make exploitation of a patented invention possible if the supplier knew (or it was sufficiently clear) that the items were suitable and intended for that use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If factors/equipment are commonly available in the market, this provision does not apply where the supplier does not induce unauthorized parties to infringe. Those legally performing permitted exceptions under Article 85(3) are not unauthorized for purposes of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by previous domestic use
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant or patentee cannot prevent persons who, in good faith, domestically used the invention on or before the application date from continuing to use it; such prior users may continue to as much as reasonably needed for their business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior-use right cannot be expanded by licensing and can only be transferred with the business. Practices regarding products offered for sale by such prior users are outside the scope of patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal monopoly-holder exceptions and compulsory-use-like mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent concerns subjects in the field of state economic enterprises with monopoly rights, the monopoly right holder’s ability to use the invention depends on patentee permission; the monopoly holder may request permission and the patentee may require the monopoly holder to take over the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Price for use or takeover is to be agreed by the parties, or determined by the court if no agreement is reached. Monopoly holders are obligated to use inventions that yield significant economic or technical benefits.
